# `uninitialized-getorput-value`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: correctness · Profile: none · Default: warning · Fixes: none · Options: none

Reports a read, in-place update, or method call through the `value_ptr` of a
`getOrPut` result before the value is assigned on the path where
`found_existing` is false.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

`getOrPut` returns pointers into the map's storage and a `found_existing`
flag. When the key was already present, `value_ptr` points at its value; when
the call inserted the key, the new slot is `undefined` and the caller must
assign it. Reading it, updating it in place (`gop.value_ptr.* += 1`) or
calling a method on it (`gop.value_ptr.append(..)`) before that assignment
uses undefined memory: a counter starts from garbage, and a container method
dereferences garbage pointers, so the mistake shows up as a wrong count or a
crash far from its cause.

## When it fires

It reports the first use of `value_ptr` from `getOrPut`, `getOrPutAdapted`,
`getOrPutContext`, `getOrPutAssumeCapacity` and their variants when that use
reads the value, through `.*`, an in-place assignment operator, a field read
or a method call, and no earlier statement in the scope mentions
`found_existing` or assigns the value. The result may be bound with `const` or
`var` or used directly, as in `(try map.getOrPut(key)).value_ptr.* += 1`.
Assigning the value or one of its fields, taking its address, calling an
`init` method on it, or passing the result or the pointer to another function
ends the check. `getOrPutValue` initializes a new value and is not reported;
use it, or assign the value when `found_existing` is false:
`if (!gop.found_existing) gop.value_ptr.* = 0;`.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
const std = @import("std");

fn count(gpa: std.mem.Allocator, counts: *std.AutoHashMapUnmanaged(u32, u32), key: u32) !void {
    const gop = try counts.getOrPut(gpa, key);
    gop.value_ptr.* += 1;
}
```
